title: A meeting scheduler that outgrows its single-office design

initial_repo.README.md:
# meetings

Team calendar helper. See git history for the design conversation.

stages.message: Build a tiny meeting scheduler for our team calendar, scheduler.py: a Scheduler class — cal.add(title, when) where when looks like '2026-03-05 14:00', and cal.list() returns (title, when) pairs, soonest first. Just us for now, one office. Write tests for it.

requirements.text: scheduler.py with a Scheduler class: add(title, when) taking 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM' strings; list() returns (title, when) pairs sorted by time

stages.message: Thanks, this has been working great. Update: we hired two people in Berlin and they keep missing meetings. Can meetings carry a timezone when we add them, like add(title, when, tz='America/New_York')? And list() should be able to show everything in whatever timezone we ask for, like list(tz='Europe/Berlin'). If someone adds a meeting without a tz, assume New York, that's where the office is. list() with no tz shows each meeting in its own timezone, and keep times in the same 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM' shape.

requirements.text: meetings carry a timezone (default America/New_York); list(tz=...) converts; list() without a tz displays in the meeting's own timezone

hidden_tests.test_stage2_tz.py:
from scheduler import Scheduler


def test_meetings_convert_between_timezones():
    s = Scheduler()
    s.add("kickoff", "2026-03-05 14:00", tz="America/New_York")
    assert s.list(tz="Europe/Berlin") == [("kickoff", "2026-03-05 20:00")]
    assert s.list(tz="UTC") == [("kickoff", "2026-03-05 19:00")]


def test_default_tz_and_sorted_display():
    s = Scheduler()
    s.add("retro", "2026-03-05 15:00")  # no tz: the New York office
    s.add("review", "2026-03-05 14:00", tz="Europe/Berlin")
    # no display tz: each meeting shows in its own timezone
    assert s.list() == [("review", "2026-03-05 14:00"),
                        ("retro", "2026-03-05 15:00")]
    assert s.list(tz="UTC") == [("review", "2026-03-05 13:00"),
                                ("retro", "2026-03-05 20:00")]

stages.message: One more thing: we have a daily standup. add(..., repeat='daily') should mark a meeting as daily, and next_dates(title, n) returns n occurrences as 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM' strings, starting from the date the meeting was added with — next_dates(title, n, tz=...) if we want them somewhere else. The standup is at 9 for the New York folks, and it should stay at 9 for them no matter what the clocks do.

requirements.text: daily repeats keep the meeting's local wall time across DST changes; next_dates(title, n, tz=None) returns n occurrence strings starting from the meeting's own date, in the meeting's tz or a requested one

from scheduler import Scheduler


def test_daily_standup_keeps_local_time_across_dst():
    s = Scheduler()
    s.add("standup", "2026-03-07 09:00", tz="America/New_York",
          repeat="daily")
    assert s.next_dates("standup", 4) == [
        "2026-03-07 09:00", "2026-03-08 09:00",
        "2026-03-09 09:00", "2026-03-10 09:00",
    ]


def test_daily_standup_in_utc_shifts_with_dst():
    s = Scheduler()
    s.add("standup", "2026-03-07 09:00", tz="America/New_York",
          repeat="daily")
    assert s.next_dates("standup", 2, tz="UTC") == [
        "2026-03-07 14:00", "2026-03-08 13:00",
    ]
